IAMA breakfast/drive radio producer for a community radio station. AMA!

My job in the morning is to structure the segments in a 3 hour grid; interviewees, songs, and talk breaks. I give a thumbs up or two when a segment makes me laugh and a frown when it missed the mark. Sometimes I jump on mics if the chemistry isn't flowing, especially when I have a brand spankin' new team.

In the afternoon it's a little more lax, pretty much make sure we don't defame anyone or start any on-air fights.

I also fold and press all of the pre prepared audio grabs for one-off segments.

A lot of the work as a producer is in pre and post production; if you don't put the hard yards in, you dont reap the rewards. I learnt this the hard way, so that every day we all get a little less shit at our jobs. :)
What's the best part of your job?

Producing is a pretty thankless job; the best part is knowing the show went off without a hitch and presenters look forward to seeing you at 5:30am. It's also pretty great to being able to liase with interviewees before they go on air, mainly pick out any jitters or hungover band members. I still haven't decided if it's worse to have someone grumpy or nervous on air. Hair of the dog all the way (but not really)(but yes really).
how does the breakfast/drive come into play? is it a morning show?

Ah! I charge the 6-9 breakfast block and then stick around for the 5pm slot in the afternoon, so they're essentially two standalone shows. The afternoon slot makes for a fun time, as there's an insanely active text line and lovely bouts of harassment whenever we play the 'wrong' music; I figure, at least they're listening!
